raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash decode TPOT **-15% at concurrency 1 on 2x DGX Spark (SM121, TP=2)** by running the BF16 decode GEMMs on the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM instead of cuBLAS. On `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` the attention projections (KDA and MLA), shared experts and LM head stay BF16 and take roughly 46 of a 68 ms decode step on cuBLAS gemv. `glm5next` has no low-latency GEMM module yet, so this adds one modelled on `qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py` (#59753, #59632, #61437) with measured SM121 skinny-GEMM plans for the TP=2 local shapes, installed from `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextMTP`. Supersedes #62949.

## Claims

- 7 local `(N, K)` shapes at M = 1/2/4 (20 entries), routed only on capability `(12, 1)`; other GPUs, dtypes, token counts and shapes keep the standard linear path (cuBLAS).
- Kernel: skinny GEMM is 1.35x to 1.73x faster than cuBLAS gemv at M=1 (238-283 GB/s vs 162-176 GB/s), 1.04x to 1.36x at M=2/4.
- End to end, no speculation, concurrency 1: TPOT 64.0 -> 54.1 ms (-15%), 15.3 -> 18.0 tok/s. With MTP k=3 the decode step is one verify pass at M=4 plus three draft passes at M=1: ITL -3.6%, TPOT -2.7%, 26.7 -> 27.8 tok/s.
- GSM8K (n=100): 93 with cuBLAS, 94 with skinny GEMM.

## Validation

Kernel, cuBLAS (`F.linear`) vs skinny GEMM through the module path on GB10 (CUDA graph replay, weight rotated out of L2, nightly 8e2beaa3bf), cosine 1.000000 between the two outputs for every entry:

| shape (N, K) | layer | M | cuBLAS (us) | skinny GEMM (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (12576, 4096) | KDA in_proj | 1 | 608 | 429 | 1.42x |
|  |  | 2 | 453 | 425 | 1.07x |
|  |  | 4 | 450 | 429 | 1.05x |
| (4096, 4096) | KDA o_proj | 1 | 203 | 137 | 1.48x |
|  |  | 2 | 147 | 136 | 1.08x |
|  |  | 4 | 148 | 140 | 1.06x |
| (2048, 4096) | shared gate_up, MLA qkv_a | 1 | 103 | 64 | 1.61x |
|  |  | 2 | 78 | 64 | 1.22x |
|  |  | 4 | 79 | 63 | 1.24x |
| (4096, 1024) | shared down | 1 | 51 | 30 | 1.73x |
|  |  | 2 | 39 | 29 | 1.34x |
|  |  | 4 | 39 | 29 | 1.36x |
| (8192, 1536) | MLA q_b | 1 | 147 | 102 | 1.44x |
|  |  | 2 | 115 | 102 | 1.13x |
|  |  | 4 | 122 | 101 | 1.20x |
| (4096, 8192) | MLA o_proj | 1 | 291 | - | not included |
|  |  | 2 | 289 | 278 | 1.04x |
|  |  | 4 | 300 | 280 | 1.07x |
| (77440, 4096) | lm_head | 1 | 3606 | 2663 | 1.35x |
|  |  | 2 | 2789 | 2655 | 1.05x |
|  |  | 4 | 2741 | 2581 | 1.06x |

These are cold-L2 numbers, which is the serving case: decode reads each weight once per step and 45 layers do not fit the 24 MB L2. Weighted by how often each shape runs in a decode step, the entries save about 13 ms per step at M=1 and 3 ms at M=2 or M=4 in the probe; the server gains 10 ms at M=1 because the GEMMs interleave with MoE and attention. MLA o_proj at M=1 is not included: cuBLAS already streams this shape at 231 GB/s (162-176 GB/s on the other shapes), so the best skinny config from the sweep gained only 3% in the module path, under the 5% bar. M=8/16 are within 2% of cuBLAS and are not listed.

End to end, cuBLAS (current main) vs skinny GEMM (this PR): `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` TP=2 on two Sparks, FP8 KV, SPEED-Bench 2K in / 1K out, 8 requests at concurrency 1, greedy (`--temperature 0`), two interleaved runs per arm (each cell lists run 1 / run 2), nightly 8e2beaa3bf:

| | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | GSM8K (n=100) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cuBLAS (main) | 64.17 / 63.83 | 63.94 / 63.68 | 15.27 / 15.33 | 93 |
| skinny GEMM (this PR) | 54.14 / 54.10 | 54.03 / 53.96 | 18.02 / 18.03 | 94 |
| change (mean of the two runs) | **-15.4%** | -15.4% | +17.8% | +1 |

With MTP k=3 (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.875 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8`, same nightly and sampling):

| | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cuBLAS (main) | 36.05 / 36.11 | 102.72 / 103.27 | 26.79 / 26.66 | 2.87 / 2.87 |
| skinny GEMM (this PR) | 35.08 / 35.16 | 99.18 / 99.41 | 27.51 / 28.02 | 2.85 / 2.90 |
| change (mean of the two runs) | -2.7% | **-3.6%** | +3.9% | +0.2% |

With MTP the ITL is the decode step (one verify pass at M=4 plus three draft passes at M=1); TPOT and tok/s divide it by the tokens accepted per step. Under greedy decoding the acceptance length stays within 2.85-2.90 across the four runs, so the step gain carries over: TPOT -2.7%, tok/s +3.9%. An earlier 4-request run at model-default sampling gave -12% without speculation (the number in the commit message); with MTP its acceptance length swung 3% between repeats, which hid the step gain.

An nsys census of the skinny GEMM arm shows every listed shape on `CuteSkinnyGemm` in the server (45% of GPU time without speculation, 39.5% with MTP); what is left on cuBLAS is KDA `f_b`/`g_b` (4096, 128) (#57617), the fp32-output router gate (288, 4096) and MLA o_proj at M=1.

Tests: `pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm5next`, 26 passed on GB10 (table validity, capability routing, hook installation, 20 selected shapes with cosine > 0.999 against `F.linear`). The selected-shape test skips off capability (12, 1), which CI does not have.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# on each DGX Spark, --node-rank 0 / 1
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \
  --master-addr 192.168.100.1 --master-port 29500 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.84 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prefix-caching --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --reasoning-parser glm45 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
# MTP k=3 arm: add --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
#   and use --gpu-memory-utilization 0.875 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8
# SPEED_BENCH_DIR holds throughput_2k.jsonl, built from nvidia/SPEED-Bench with NeMo-Skills prepare.py
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path $SPEED_BENCH_DIR --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_2k \
  --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --num-warmups 2 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1 \
  --temperature 0 --seed 0
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm5next
```

</details>

## Details

- Plans come from a CUDA-graph sweep over block_size, outputs_per_block, k_unroll, vector_width and static_k with the weight rotated out of L2, keeping entries that beat cuBLAS by more than 5%. `(2048, 4096)` serves both the shared-expert gate/up and the MLA fused q_a/kv_a projection.
- The replacement method follows the quant method the layer carries: a quant config that excludes `lm_head` gives `ParallelLMHead` an `UnquantizedLinearMethod` rather than an `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, and the head stayed on cuBLAS until this was handled.
- Not covered: TP=1 (the model does not fit one Spark), KDA `f_b`/`g_b` `(4096, 128)` (#57617), MTP `eh_proj` (a plain `nn.Linear`), and M=3, which uses cuBLAS.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the sweep scripts, the module and the tests; all code and measurements were reviewed and run by the author.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

nodes.body:
Thanks for the PR. I tried a different structure on [LopezCastroRoberto:glm5next-skinny-gemm-cleanup](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/compare/main...LopezCastroRoberto:vllm:glm5next-skinny-gemm-cleanup?expand=1). It drops `layers/low_latency_gemm.py` and the `GLM5Next` installer. Instead, as in `GateLinear`, each unquantized layer checks its own `(N, K)` against a shape-keyed plan table. This should keep your SM121 numbers unchanged, but please double-check and cherry-pick if looks good to you.

Matching layers then go through one custom op inside the CUDA unquantized GEMM path. GLM code stays untouched, `lm_head` is covered, and `--linear-backend` is respected. Because plans are keyed by weight shape, on SM121 any layer with a listed shape uses them and benefits from it, not just GLM’s. 

This refactor also lets Qwen4Exp’s copied op and installer (`qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py`) become table entries, and the plain skinny GEMM projections in GLM-5.2 (`deepseek_v32/nvidia/glm52_low_latency_gemm.py`) and Kimi-K3 (`kimi_k3/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py`) move onto the same path in follow-up PRs.

`_warmup_skinny_gemm` mirrors `_warmup_ll_bf16_router_gemm`, but queues configs through `request_warmup_configs` for `cutedsl_warmup()` to compile, because `ShapeDynamicSkinnyGemm` is still on the deprecated CuTe DSL provider registry. Compiling directly with `.warmup(shapes=..., m_values=...)` like `ll_bf16` needs its `VllmJitKernel` migration ([vllm-project/vllm#49349](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49349)), which also touches Kimi-K3, GLM-5.2 and Qwen4Exp, so it is left for a follow-up too.

- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the sweep scripts, the module and the tests; all code and measurements were reviewed and run by the author.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Measured skinny GEMM plans for unquantized BF16 linear layers.
+
+Plans are keyed by device capability, local ``(N, K)`` weight shape and token
+count. A layer whose shape is listed runs the planned config for that token
+count; other token counts use ``F.linear``. Entries are kept only where the
+skinny GEMM beats cuBLAS by more than 5% under CUDA graph replay.
+"""
+
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.cute_dsl.skinny_gemm import (
+    SkinnyGemmConfig,
+    shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+SkinnyGemmPlan = dict[int, SkinnyGemmConfig]
+
+# DGX Spark (GB10), measured on GLM-5.3-Flash local shapes at TP=2.
+SM121_SKINNY_GEMM_PLANS: dict[tuple[int, int], SkinnyGemmPlan] = {
+    # Shared-expert fused gate/up and MLA fused q_a/kv_a projections.
+    (2048, 4096): {
+        1: SkinnyGemmConfig(1, 32, 1, k_unroll=4, static_k=4096),
+        2: SkinnyGemmConfig(2, 64, 1, k_unroll=4, vector_width=4, static_k=4096),
+        4: SkinnyGemmConfig(4, 128, 1, vector_width=2, static_k=4096),
+    },
+    # Shared-expert down projection.
+    (4096, 1024): {
+        1: SkinnyGemmConfig(1, 64, 1, vector_width=2, static_k=1024),
+        2: SkinnyGemmConfig(2, 64, 1, vector_width=2, static_k=1024),
+        4: SkinnyGemmConfig(4, 64, 1, vector_width=2, static_k=1024),
+    },
+    # KDA output projection.
+    (4096, 4096): {
+        1: SkinnyGemmConfig(1, 32, 2, k_unroll=4, vector_width=4, static_k=4096),
+        2: SkinnyGemmConfig(2, 64, 1, k_unroll=4, vector_width=2, static_k=4096),
+        4: SkinnyGemmConfig(4, 64, 1, vector_width=2, static_k=4096),
+    },
+    # MLA output projection.
+    (4096, 8192): {
+        2: SkinnyGemmConfig(2, 64, 2, k_unroll=2, vector_width=2, static_k=8192),
+        4: SkinnyGemmConfig(4, 256, 1, k_unroll=2, static_k=8192),
+    },
+    # MLA q_b projection.
+    (8192, 1536): {
+        1: SkinnyGemmConfig(1, 32, 1, k_unroll=4, vector_width=2, static_k=1536),
+        2: SkinnyGemmConfig(2, 32, 1, k_unroll=2, vector_width=2, static_k=1536),
+        4: SkinnyGemmConfig(4, 32, 1, k_unroll=2, vector_width=2, static_k=1536),
+    },
+    # KDA fused QKV/beta/f_a/g_a input projection.
+    (12576, 4096): {
+        1: SkinnyGemmConfig(1, 256, 1, k_unroll=2, vector_width=2),
+        2: SkinnyGemmConfig(2, 256, 1),
+        4: SkinnyGemmConfig(4, 128, 1, k_unroll=4, vector_width=4, static_k=4096),
+    },
+    # LM head.
+    (77440, 4096): {
+        1: SkinnyGemmConfig(1, 256, 1, static_k=4096),
+        2: SkinnyGemmConfig(2, 256, 1, k_unroll=2),
+        4: SkinnyGemmConfig(4, 256, 1, k_unroll=2),
+    },
+}
+
+SKINNY_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY: dict[
+    tuple[int, int] | None, dict[tuple[int, int], SkinnyGemmPlan]
+] = {
+    (12, 1): SM121_SKINNY_GEMM_PLANS,
+}
+
+
+def get_skinny_gemm_plan(n: int, k: int) -> SkinnyGemmPlan | None:
+    """Return the token-count plan for an ``(N, K)`` weight on this device."""
+    plans = SKINNY_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY.get(
+        current_platform.get_device_capability()
+    )
+    if plans is None or not shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm.is_available():
+        return None
+    return plans.get((n, k))

+def cuda_skinny_unquantized_gemm_impl(
+    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.cute_dsl.skinny_gemm import (
+        row_stride_ok,
+        shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.cute_dsl.skinny_gemm_plans import (
+        get_skinny_gemm_plan,
+    )
+
+    plan = get_skinny_gemm_plan(weight.shape[0], weight.shape[1])
+    config = None if plan is None else plan.get(x.shape[0])
+    if (
+        config is not None
+        and x.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and weight.is_cuda
+        and weight.is_contiguous()
+        and row_stride_ok(x, config)
+    ):
+        return shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm(x, weight, config)
+    return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight)
+
+
+def cuda_skinny_unquantized_gemm_fake(
+    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return x.new_empty((*x.shape[:-1], weight.shape[0]))
+
+
+direct_register_custom_op(
+    op_name="cuda_skinny_unquantized_gemm",
+    op_func=cuda_skinny_unquantized_gemm_impl,
+    fake_impl=cuda_skinny_unquantized_gemm_fake,
+)
+
+
+def maybe_use_skinny_gemm(layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+    """Mark ``layer`` for the skinny GEMM if its weight shape has a plan."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.cute_dsl.skinny_gemm_plans import (
+        get_skinny_gemm_plan,
+    )
+
+    weight = layer.weight
+    if weight.ndim != 2:
+        return
+
+    if (
+        not envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
+        and weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and getattr(layer, "bias", None) is None
+        and get_skinny_gemm_plan(*weight.shape) is not None
+    ):
+        layer.use_skinny_gemm = True
+
+
+def cuda_unquantized_gemm(
+    layer: torch.nn.Module,
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # The op picks the config from the token count at runtime, so the choice
+    # stays out of the compiled graph.
+    if (
+        bias is None
+        and getattr(layer, "use_skinny_gemm", False)
+        and x.is_cuda
+        and x.dim() == 2
+    ):
+        return torch.ops.vllm.cuda_skinny_unquantized_gemm(x, weight)
+    return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, bias)
+

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
Overall LGTM. Left two mostly cosmetic suggestions.

Thanks for the PR. I tried a different structure on [LopezCastroRoberto:glm5next-skinny-gemm-cleanup](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/compare/main...LopezCastroRoberto:vllm:glm5next-skinny-gemm-cleanup?expand=1). It drops `layers/low_latency_gemm.py` and the `GLM5Next` installer. Instead, as in `GateLinear`, each unquantized layer checks its own `(N, K)` against a shape-keyed plan table. This should keep your SM121 numbers unchanged, but please double-check and cherry-pick if looks good to you.

Matching layers then go through one custom op inside the CUDA unquantized GEMM path. GLM code stays untouched, `lm_head` is covered, and `--linear-backend` is respected. Because plans are keyed by weight shape, on SM121 any layer with a listed shape uses them and benefits from it, not just GLM’s. 

This refactor also lets Qwen4Exp’s copied op and installer (`qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py`) become table entries, and the plain skinny GEMM projections in GLM-5.2 (`deepseek_v32/nvidia/glm52_low_latency_gemm.py`) and Kimi-K3 (`kimi_k3/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py`) move onto the same path in follow-up PRs.

`_warmup_skinny_gemm` mirrors `_warmup_ll_bf16_router_gemm`, but queues configs through `request_warmup_configs` for `cutedsl_warmup()` to compile, because `ShapeDynamicSkinnyGemm` is still on the deprecated CuTe DSL provider registry. Compiling directly with `.warmup(shapes=..., m_values=...)` like `ll_bf16` needs its `VllmJitKernel` migration ([vllm-project/vllm#49349](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49349)), which also touches Kimi-K3, GLM-5.2 and Qwen4Exp, so it is left for a follow-up too.
